## Design

### 2026-10-12 – ### What I worked on

**4h**

### What I worked on
Modeled and verified the primary two-piece protective enclosure for the SmartCurtain controller, designing both the main chassis and the top lid to house the pcb and the stepper motor

### CAD Assembly and PCB footprint referencing
  - Imported the 3D STEP model exported from KiCad into the CAD workspace to extract precise component bounding boxes, connector alignments, and standoff pitches.
  - Applied a 0.35mm horizontal clearance offset between the PCB perimeter and internal enclosure walls to account for FDM thermal shrinkage and board fabrication tolerances.

### Main Bottom Enclosure
  - Parameterized structural wall thickness to 2.4mm (ensuring an exact multiple of 6 solid perimeters with a 0.4mm nozzle for maximum rigidity).
  - Modeled 4 external cylindrical screw pillars with countersunk bores sized for M3 fasteners and brass heat-set threaded inserts.
  - Integrated lower terminal access windows for all 4 screw terminal blocks (stepper phases and sensor interfaces) using 45-degree peaked roofs, completely eliminating the need for internal support material during 3D printing.
  - Created a recessed cutout for the USB-C port with a 1.0mm relief pocket to ensure wide USB-C cable overmolds seat fully into the receptacle.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/32fff56f6c89cf9a9a509fd416cc052d4bf0556de88415043d3acc6b7927679b.png)

### Top Enclosure Lid
  - Modeled a dedicated top shell with self-aligning recessed mating lips to interface securely with the bottom chassis.
  - Added directional ventilation slots directly above the TMC2209 StepStick socket to enable passive convective airflow across the driver heatsink.
  - Placed concentric pass-through cutouts for the EC11 rotary encoder control shaft and the 5mm 940nm IR emitter LED.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/ed511435a94c52bb74fb88ac630955ac7379a053356b573f34dc71bb3ae29288.png)

### What broke and how I fixed it
- Rectangular terminal block cutouts originally required fragile support structures that would have been tedious to clean out; redesigned the upper edge of every side opening with 45-degree chamfers so the slicer can bridge cleanly without any print supports.
-Sharp right-angle junctions between the corner mounting pillars and the main outer walls showed high shear stress risks; added generous filleted ribs along the pillar seams to prevent layer delamination under fastener torque.
